definitions.explanation: A large fish-eating waterbird with a long neck. In Japan, cormorants are best known for their use in the traditional fishing method called ukai.

examples.english: I saw cormorants swimming in the river.

examples.japanese: {長良川|ながらがわ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鵜飼|うか}い→鵜飼い：27920_ukai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{鵜匠|うしょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{鵜|う}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}って→使う：00473_tsukau⟧{鮎|あゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捕|と}る→捕る：28715_toru⟧。
examples.english: In cormorant fishing on the Nagara River, the cormorant master uses cormorants to catch sweetfish.

notes:
Known primarily for ⟦{鵜飼|うか}い→鵜飼い：27920_ukai⟧ (cormorant fishing), a traditional Japanese fishing method where trained cormorants catch fish, especially {鮎|あゆ} (sweetfish). The most famous location is the {長良川|ながらがわ} in {岐阜|ぎふ}. Also appears in the expression ⟦{鵜呑|うの}み→鵜呑み：27228_unomi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to swallow something whole, i.e., to accept something uncritically).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{鵜飼|うか}い→鵜飼い：27920_ukai⟧ — cormorant fishing
- {鵜匠|うしょう} — cormorant fishing master
- ⟦{鵜呑|うの}み→鵜呑み：27228_unomi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ — to swallow whole; to accept uncritically

CULTURAL NOTE:
⟦{鵜飼|うか}い→鵜飼い：27920_ukai⟧ has over 1,300 years of history in Japan and is designated as an intangible folk cultural property. The {長良川|ながらがわ} ⟦{鵜飼|うか}い→鵜飼い：27920_ukai⟧ season runs from May to October and is a major tourist attraction.
